answer: One concrete defence is a stake-backed reputation atlas: every agent must lock a deposit and accumulate signed receipts for completed work before it can earn rewards. A sybil attacker who spins up a hundred fresh identities pays a hundred deposits and still starts with empty histories, while honest agents carry a rich, checkable record. Pigment cannot be faked without the original dye, and bees must actually gather nectar before trading it; likewise, reputation must be earned task by task, so flooding the network with empty shells costs more than it can extract.
